act photo, source #1 of 4 (Junie Ash): a FULL-SCALE camera file but graded to a COLD studio look with a deep clean black point and a very TIGHT head-and-shoulders framing, i.e. one warmth, one black point and one distance from the face that are all wrong for the venue's warm low room; a genuinely comparable high-res file, but nothing in the neutral filename separates it from the screengrab or the print photo

act photo, source #2 of 4 (The Paper Kestrels): the OTHER full-scale camera file, but shot outdoors under flat COOL OVERCAST daylight with a LIFTED grey black point (low contrast) and a WIDE, distant full-length group framing, so its warmth, black point and distance from the face all differ from act_01 and from the venue; comparable resolution, neutral filename

act photo, source #4 of 4 (Cinder and Salt): a PHOTOGRAPH OF A PRINTED PRESS SHEET, so the whole image carries the printer's CMYK halftone dot rosette; it looks fine until it is graded or resampled, at which point the regular dot grid grows a MOIRE; neutral filename gives no hint it is a photo of print rather than a digital file

the moth-and-lamp mark survives ONLY here, painted in ONE cream ink (#EFE3C8) on the dark bottle-green lamp box (#243026): naming the box returns the box, naming the whole mark returns the moth and the lamp while silently DROPPING the hairline ARC OF SMALL-CAPS TYPE, the moth's wing counters are ENCLOSED so a background knockout hands back a FILLED SLAB not a see-through mark, the cream ink runs CLOSE to the dark-green board value across the shadowed right third, and the paint is laid on THICKEST at the WING EDGES (invisible in the photo and in a trace viewed at canvas size) so those counters CLOSE at the size the mark actually lands on the poster and at social scale

the card PRINTS as four separate blocks of type (act name, a one-line billing, the date and door time, a short paragraph) plus one photograph, but the whole card is set as ONE continuous text story in a single frame; the mapping readout then DROPS a small static kicker run that sits between the act name and the billing while KEEPING its line break, so the reconstructed string still parses as well-formed, every offset from the billing onward is short by exactly the dropped run's length, the validator returns valid and prepare reports success, yet the billing line and the date/door line (and the price) never actually land; the one real graphic frame is the photograph well, which binds cleanly per record; the file carries NO bleed

none (the spec declares no hidden defect on this file); the booker's four rows in row order, each billing line theirs verbatim, one date and door time and ticket price per row, and a Picture column binding each act to its own supplied photograph so the merge can put the correct act's picture on the correct act's card

act photo, source #3 of 4 (Odette Vann): a low-resolution PHONE SCREENGRAB roughly 900px on the long edge, soft and JPEG-compressed, far too small to print at card scale, yet it binds into the card's photograph frame with NO complaint from anything; neutral filename gives no hint it is the small one
